notes.subject: plate
notes.text: Long white plates with the blue EU strip on the left; taxis have yellow plates.

notes.subject: language
notes.text: Å, Ä and Ö all appear. Finnish also has Ä and Ö but long words with double vowels; Danish and Norwegian lack Ä and Ö.

notes.subject: line
notes.text: Outer lines on small roads are white, dashed and shorter than in Norway. All lines are white.

notes.subject: line
notes.text: Highway edge lines look solid from afar but are split into small sections; in Denmark the sections are rectangular.

notes.subject: bollard
notes.text: Black and white bollards, usually with a grey reflector (orange at intersections): wedge, round or thin and curved.

notes.subject: pole
notes.text: Orange snow poles with a tall white reflector just above the middle, sometimes with a second thin one.

notes.subject: pole
notes.text: Wooden utility poles with a small black metal cap on top, found only in Nordic countries; lamps sit just below the top.

notes.subject: pole
notes.text: Wooden markers with a blue and a white stripe at the top stand near poles and pylons, found nowhere else in the region.

notes.subject: sign
notes.text: Pedestrian signs have four stripes, and one version shows a female figure.

notes.subject: sign
notes.text: Directions are mostly blue with white text and a thin arrow; small places get yellow signs with a red border.

notes.subject: sign
notes.text: Yellow arrows on a blue background, unique in Europe apart from very rare ones in Luxembourg.

notes.subject: sign
notes.text: Small roads have blue signs with a large white M (passing place); the Norwegian font is different.

notes.subject: sign
notes.text: Signposts often carry striped markings: blue-white or red-yellow, and other mixes, almost unique here.

notes.subject: sign
notes.text: Road signs and roadworks gear are often red and yellow, even chevrons.

notes.subject: language
notes.text: Street names end in vägen or gatan, often shortened to v and g; Norway attaches gata, Denmark uses vej and gade.

notes.subject: architecture
notes.text: Rural houses are mostly wooden and painted a dark red, also seen in Norway and Finland.

notes.subject: architecture
notes.text: Cities are modern, concrete and brick; suburbs are free-standing single-family houses.

notes.subject: vegetation
notes.text: Boreal forest, small to medium farms and many lakes; mountainous north and west, flatter south and east.

notes.subject: street
notes.text: Traditional fence of thin spaced vertical trunks with slanting trunks stacked on top.

notes.subject: car
notes.text: Volvo is almost 30% of cars here, three times the share in the neighbouring countries.

notes.subject: other
notes.text: Church flag with a red cross on yellow and a crown in the middle, often near churches.

notes.subject: car
notes.text: A white camera car with a long antenna on much older coverage, also found in Iceland and Finland.

notes.subject: car
notes.text: Newer coverage comes from a red, a white and a blue car, with or without a visible antenna.

notes.subject: vegetation
notes.text: The most open farmland, with only small tree patches and more varied crops than elsewhere.

notes.subject: landscape
notes.text: Round exposed rocks with small bushes on top are common on the west coast.

notes.subject: landscape
notes.text: White sand beside roads and fences of wedge-cut trunks mark Gotland.

notes.subject: landscape
notes.text: Extremely flat, with many small rock walls and small bushes.

notes.subject: street
notes.text: Red dirt roads and thin pines are typical of western Dalarna.

notes.subject: vegetation
notes.text: Thin, weak-looking boreal trees on sandy soil in the far north; treeless mountains only in the northwest.

notes.subject: architecture
notes.text: White stone or red brick houses with a coloured wooden gable triangle, and half-timbered houses in the south.

notes.subject: architecture
notes.text: Limestone houses with dirty-white facades, and distinctive churches with grey walls and small paired windows.

notes.subject: architecture
notes.text: Big, long red farmhouses on 2-3 floors with many large windows.

notes.subject: architecture
notes.text: Light white and pale yellow houses along the coast between Gothenburg and the Norwegian border.

notes.subject: sign
notes.text: Bilingual signs in Sámi appear inland in the north; Meänkieli names ending in väylä appear near the Finnish border.

notes.subject: sign
notes.text: All street signs in Gothenburg are blue and almost always two lines.

notes.subject: sign
notes.text: Street signs with two rows split by a black line and no black border belong to the capital.

notes.subject: street
notes.text: Cobbled streets, small painted stone houses, roses on walls and an old Hanseatic wall mark the town of Visby.
